prose.hook: Bulgaria sits in southeastern Europe on the Black Sea, wedged between Romania and Turkey, a position that has long put it astride key land routes linking Europe to the Middle East and Asia and close to the strategically important Turkish Straits.
prose.physicalGeography: The country is dominated by mountainous terrain, with lowlands confined mainly to the north and southeast. Its Black Sea coastline anchors its position between Romania and Turkey.
prose.climate: Bulgaria has a temperate climate marked by cold, damp winters and hot, dry summers. The country is also subject to earthquakes and landslides.
prose.economy: Bulgaria is an upper-middle-income economy within the EU, with its currency pegged to the euro while eurozone accession remains pending. Declining energy prices have helped lower inflation, and EU structural funds are supporting a recovery in investment, though the labor force faces shortages of skilled workers due to emigration and an aging population. Its industries span electricity, gas, and water; food, beverages, and tobacco; and machinery, automotive parts, metals, chemicals, coke, refined petroleum, and nuclear fuel, alongside outsourcing centers, while its main exports are refined petroleum, garments, refined copper, wheat, and natural gas.
prose.peopleAndCulture: Bulgarians make up 78.5% of the population, with Turkish (7.8%) and Roma (4.1%) minorities alongside smaller other groups. Religiously, most identify as Christian (64.7%), with a Muslim minority of 9.8%, while roughly a fifth of the population leaves religious affiliation unspecified.
